pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Best practice when working on Rhythm: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Rhythm.
   B. Damage equipment used for Rhythm.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Rhythm.
   D. Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

2. Best practice when working on Javelin and Sculpture: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Javelin and Sculpture.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Javelin and Sculpture.
   C. Practise Javelin and Sculpture with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Damage equipment used for Javelin and Sculpture.

3. Warming up before sport helps to: (1 mark)
   A. Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk
   B. Replace drinking water
   C. Remove the need for rules
   D. Guarantee a trophy

4. Best practice when working on Kenyan Indigenous Games: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Kenyan Indigenous Games.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Kenyan Indigenous Games.
   C. Practise Kenyan Indigenous Games with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Kenyan Indigenous Games.

5. Best practice when working on Descant Recorder: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Descant Recorder.
   B. Practise Descant Recorder with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Descant Recorder.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Descant Recorder.

6. Best practice when working on Melody: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Melody.
   B. Damage equipment used for Melody.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Melody.
   D. Practise Melody with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

7. Primary colours are: (1 mark)
   A. Green, orange, and purple
   B. Black, white, and grey
   C. Brown, pink, and gold
   D. Red, blue, and yellow

8. Best practice when working on Swimming: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Swimming with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Damage equipment used for Swimming.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Swimming.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Swimming.

9. Best practice when working on Drawing and Painting: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Drawing and Painting.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Drawing and Painting.
   C. Damage equipment used for Drawing and Painting.
   D. Practise Drawing and Painting with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

10. Best practice when working on Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork.
   C. Damage equipment used for Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork.

11. Best practice when working on Components of Creative Arts and Sports: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Components of Creative Arts and Sports with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Damage equipment used for Components of Creative Arts and Sports.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Components of Creative Arts and Sports.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Components of Creative Arts and Sports.

12. Best practice when working on Storytelling and Animation: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Storytelling and Animation.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Storytelling and Animation.
   C. Practise Storytelling and Animation with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Storytelling and Animation.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Drawing and Painting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Swimming and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Kenyan Indigenous Games and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

2. C — Practise Javelin and Sculpture with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

3. A — Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk

4. C — Practise Kenyan Indigenous Games with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

5. B — Practise Descant Recorder with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

6. D — Practise Melody with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

7. D — Red, blue, and yellow

8. A — Practise Swimming with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

9. D — Practise Drawing and Painting with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

10. A — Practise Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

11. A — Practise Components of Creative Arts and Sports with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

12. C — Practise Storytelling and Animation with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Drawing and Painting; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Swimming; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Kenyan Indigenous Games; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
